report.source_text:
The patient was undertaken for excision and curettage (Figure 5) of the lesion (black arrow), following which the cavity in the anterior aspect of the tibia was plugged with hydroxyapatite bone blocks and sealed with bone wax (green arrow). Postoperative X-rays confirmed the adequate filling of the cavity with no evidence of breakage in the bone.
Postoperative physiotherapy was started, and the patient had no postoperative complications. Suture removal was done on post-op day 12, and the patient was subsequently discharged and advised for regular follow-up.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 17-year-old boy presented with a four-year history of dull aching pain and swelling in the right leg, with a prior tibia fracture two years earlier. Radiographic imaging revealed a well-defined expansile lytic-sclerotic lesion with septations in the proximal tibia. Biopsy and histopathological examination showed a combination of epithelial and fibrous mesenchymal cells with epithelial nests arranged in a palisading pattern. The histopathological features confirmed the diagnosis of adamantinoma. The lesion was surgically excised and curetted followed by bone grafting, with an uneventful postoperative course and no complications.

Histopathology showed a combination of epithelial and fibrous mesenchymal cells with epithelial nests arranged in a palisading pattern.
Histopathological features confirmed the diagnosis of adamantinoma.
The patient underwent excision and curettage of the lesion with bone grafting and had an uneventful postoperative course.
